subject: Outcome Contract: pass/fail gates, safety nets, and test fixtures for 6-week MAP
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@carewell.health>, Alicia Park <alicia.park@carewell.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Outcome Contract: pass/fail gates, safety nets, and test fixtures for 6-week MAP

Hi Tom / Alicia —

As we discussed on Friday, attached is a short "Outcome Contract" for the 6-week mutual action plan (MAP) so both teams have a single source of truth for what constitutes success and the decision points for cutover. The goal here is to keep acceptance criteria crisp and testable so your internal stakeholders can sign off quickly.

Key summary (high level):
- Acceptance window: 6 weeks from pilot go-live (target start: week of 3/8).
- Primary success metric: Production-style recall on structured extraction tasks >= 92% on CareWell validation set (see tab "KPI thresholds" in workbook).
- Safety stop-gate: Any single-day regression > 6 absolute points on recall triggers pause and investigation.
- Latency SLA (P95): <= 350ms for 1-2 token completions on typical queries; excused for long-burst workloads documented in playbook.
- Data residency & audit: telemetry retention 90 days, access logs exported weekly.

Acceptance tests and owners (examples):
- Functional correctness: set of 120 canonical test cases (Acceptance owner: CareWell QA / contact Alicia).
- Edge-case sampling: 1,000 random production-like requests evaluated for hallucination rate (owner: Redwood Test Ops, Ben).
- Load smoke: 10k tokens/min sustained for 30 minutes with no errors > 0.5% (owner: Redwood Infra, Karthik).
- Security checklist: SOC 2 evidence bundle + encryption proof (owner: CareWell security and Redwood ops).

Attachments: outcome contract draft (PDF) and acceptance test cases (Excel) — please review the KPI thresholds tab.

Ask for this week:
1) Please confirm the primary stakeholders who will sign acceptance (functional, security, procurement).
2) Confirm the earliest pilot start date (we tentatively have week of 3/8).
3) Any immediate concerns about the stop-gate thresholds above?

If you prefer, we can convert this into a short mutual action checklist (Milestone + owner + sign-off) and spin up a shared Drive checklist for approvals.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

--
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs:
- carewell-outcome-contract-draft.pdf (PDF, 28 KB)
- acceptance-test-cases-CAREWELL.xlsx (XLSX, 46 KB)

Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Outcome Contract: pass/fail gates, safety nets, and test fixtures for 6-week MAP

Thanks Sofia — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) The 92% recall threshold — is that measured against our annotated validation set (the one we shared last quarter) or an augmented set Redwood will generate? We need to ensure we and our regulators can reproduce the metric.
2) The single-day regression stop-gate is okay in principle; can we make it a 48-hour rolling window so we don't trigger on transient spikes?
3) Who signs operational acceptance vs. legal/procurement sign-off? Alicia will represent product/QA. Legal will need to review the outcome contract wording and the retention clauses.

Also cc'ing our Legal team for their review. If possible, please include a short test fixture listing (minimal repro steps) for each canonical test case — that helps our QA.

Tom
Director, Product Ops | CareWell Health
tom@carewell.health | +1 (617) 555-2244

Tom — thanks for the quick read. Two notes from engineering/test ops perspective: 

- Measurement reproducibility: we will run the 92% recall against your annotated validation set; Redwood will provide all evaluation code and deterministic seed values so you can re-run. We'll add a small appendix to the PDF with the exact evaluation script and environment (Python + requirements.txt).

- Stop-gate window: 48-hour rolling window is reasonable — recommend we make the trigger ">= 5 absolute points drop averaged across a 48-hour rolling window". That reduces noise while keeping sensitivity.

- Test fixtures: attached XLSX already has a "repro steps" column; I'll expand it with exact curl commands and example payloads by EOD Wed.

Operational fallback plan (short):
1) Canary variant (lower-quantized model) auto-routed for 10% traffic for 48 hours after deploy.
2) If regression persists, automatic rollback to previous validated model and immediate incident postmortem.

I'll also include a short cost delta estimate for enabling continuous evaluation on the validation stream (roughly +6% on monthly token cost for the pilot).

Ben

- Add a sign-off matrix page: stakeholder, role, acceptance criteria they authorize, and electronic sign-off column. That reduces back-and-forth during close.
- Include runbook owners for the canary/rollback steps (Ben owns test ops; Karthik owns infra).
- For procurement: flag any committed reserved capacity implications (I expect Karthik's note on cost deltas will feed into that).

Sofia — please set a 30-minute review with CareWell Legal to go through the retention language and the definition of "telemetry". Alicia / Tom — can you propose two 30-minute slots on Thursday or Friday so we can get legal on the line?

Once legal has minor edits, we can convert the PDF to a DocuSign envelope and route for signatures.

- Canary plan: we'll schedule a staged rollout policy in Deployment Manager (10% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h windows) with automated canary metrics (recall, latency, error-rate). If canary metrics deviate beyond thresholds, the system will auto-rollback. Owner: Karthik Iyer (Infra).
- Reserved capacity: if CareWell wants guaranteed throughput we can propose a 3-month dedicated pool with pre-warmed instances; I'll attach a brief delta sheet to the Drive folder (link above).
- Cost note: Ben's continuous evaluation + dedicated pool combined ~ +12-18% ARR impact for pilot months only; exact depends on token volume.
